code.tree_clean_means: git status --porcelain -- pipeline tests PREANALYSIS.md, run in the gizmo folder, printed nothing (untracked files included), so the commit is the code that ran
code.code_identity_means: git rev-parse --verify HEAD:./<path>, run in the gizmo folder, for pipeline, tests and PREANALYSIS.md: the git tree id of pipeline and of tests and the blob id of the plan at the commit. An id depends only on the content under its path, so with tree_clean true the three ids are the code and the plan that ran, whatever else the repository's commit holds. A resumed run is refused unless all three equal the manifest's (Joe, 2026-11-20, D-122: "Compare code identity"); the commit is recorded and not compared

body.plan_section: Electricity: the main estimate, Weights ('the same estimate weighted by each host's residential customers in its reference year'; Joe, 2026-11-19, D-105)
body.builder: design.build_with_rules under the headline rules; each host's residential customers in its reference year from side.q (res_customers), on every row of its sub-experiment (weighted_fit.customer_weights)
body.estimator: weighted_fit.weighted_fit (weighted least squares on the kernel's own regressors, inference_check.fixed_parts on outcome_analysis.stackable; point estimate only, no range), with the nominal customer weight shares and the effective contributions to the weighted headline reported apart, the effective contribution shown as the own-row headline weight (its definition accepted by Joe on 2026-11-19, D-111)
labels: descriptive: the customer-weighted point estimate, with no range (the selected inference procedure has no path that takes weights and was not validated with them; Joe, 2026-11-19, D-105)
not applicable: a descriptive point estimate with no range, so no validation is claimed (None is kept for the validated headline alone)

headline_set at 2%.label: descriptive: the customer-weighted point estimate, with no range (the selected inference procedure has no path that takes weights and was not validated with them; Joe, 2026-11-19, D-105)
headline_set at 2%.no_range: no range is reported: the selected procedure (CR2, Satterthwaite) was validated on the unweighted headline design and has no weighted path
headline_set at 2%.validation: not applicable: a descriptive point estimate with no range, so no validation is claimed (None is kept for the validated headline alone)
headline_set at 2%.outcome_alignment: checked: the vector was built by outcome_vector for exactly the rows this fit stacks
headline_set at 2%.weights: each host's residential customers in its reference year, on every row of its sub-experiment
headline_set at 2%.nominal_label: nominal customer share (each host's reference-year residential customers over all stacked hosts')
headline_set at 2%.nominal_definition: Nominal customer share. Each stacked host's residential customers in its reference year (cohort - 3), over the sum of those customers across the stacked hosts; the shares add to 1. It is computed from the customer counts alone, before any regression. Every row of a host's sub-experiment (its own rows and its matched comparison utilities' rows) carries that host's customers as its weight, so the nominal share is the weight the specification gives the host's whole sub-experiment relative to the others. It is not the weight the fitted headline places on the host (that is the effective contribution), it is not a measure of statistical influence on the estimate, it is not leverage, and it is not how far the estimate would move without the host.
headline_set at 2%.effective_label: own-row headline weight (the share of the weighted headline's weight on host rows in event years 2 and 3 that falls on this host's own rows)
headline_set at 2%.effective_definition: Effective contribution, shown as the own-row headline weight. The weighted headline is a fixed linear combination of the outcome rows, headline = omega'y, with omega = W X~ (X~'W X~)^-1 combo: W holds the customer weights on every stacked row, X~ is the regressors (the event-time columns on host rows, the degree-day columns and the gas-share controls) with the fixed effects removed under those weights, and combo takes the mean of event years 2 and 3. A host's effective contribution is the sum of omega over that host's own rows in event years 2 and 3 (its rows in its own sub-experiment, not its matched comparison utilities' rows). Across the stacked hosts these sums add to exactly 1, because omega'X equals combo' and the event-time columns are the indicators of host rows by event year. It is therefore the share of the weighted headline's total weight on host rows in event years 2 and 3 that falls on that host's own rows. It is a signed share and can be negative or larger than the host's nominal share. In exact terms, if every outcome value on the host's own rows in event years 2 and 3 rose by the same amount c and nothing else changed, the weighted headline would rise by c times the host's effective contribution. It is computed from the design's regressors, its fixed effects and the customer weights alone; no outcome, price, revenue or bill enters, and it is the same whatever the outcome. It is not a measure of statistical influence on the estimate, it is not leverage (the diagonal of the fit's hat matrix), and it is not how far the estimate would move if the host were left out: each of those depends on the outcomes or on a refit without the host, and none of them is computed here. With every weight equal it is the unweighted fit's host weight (outcome_analysis.host_weights). That the host's own rows in event years 2 and 3 are what is summed, read from 'the implied weight on its own treated rows', was accepted by Joe on 2026-11-19 (D-111) with this definition. This definition supersedes the earlier phrase 'effective regression contributions' (Joe, 2026-11-19, D-105) where the two differ: the quantity is a share of the headline's weight on host rows, computed from the design before any outcome, and not a contribution of the host's data to the estimate in any sense that depends on the outcome.
